title: Yevgeny Prigozhin

fields.label: Position held
fields.value: Leader of the Wagner Group, commanding officer

summary: Yevgeny Viktorovich Prigozhin (1 June 1961 – 23 August 2023) was a Russian mercenary leader and oligarch known for his leadership of the Wagner Group, a private military company involved in the conflict in Ukraine. He was a significant figure in the Russian military operations and political landscape, particularly regarding Russia's actions in Ukraine and his connections to the Kremlin.

sections.heading: Background and Early Life
paragraphs: Yevgeny Viktorovich Prigozhin was born on 1 June 1961 in Leningrad, [[soviet-union|Soviet Union]] (now Saint Petersburg, Russia). He was raised in a family with a military background, as his grandfather served in the Red Army during World War II. Prigozhin spent part of his childhood in Zhovti Vody, [[ukraine|Ukraine]], where he worked in an open-pit uranium mine.
Prigozhin graduated from Leningrad Sports Boarding School No. 62 in 1977, aspiring to be a professional skier. However, an injury led him to abandon this career and work as a fitness trainer.

sections.heading: Criminal History and Imprisonment
paragraphs: In 1979, Prigozhin was convicted of theft and received a suspended sentence. His criminal activities escalated, leading to a twelve-year sentence in a high-security penal colony for robbery and fraud. He served nine years before being released in 1990, after which he attempted to pursue a degree in pharmaceuticals but did not complete his studies.

sections.heading: Rise to Prominence
paragraphs: After his release, Prigozhin entered the food industry, initially selling hot dogs and later establishing a successful restaurant business. His connections with Russian political leaders, including [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]], grew during this time, leading to lucrative government contracts for his catering businesses.
By 2012, Prigozhin's companies were awarded significant contracts, including a $1.2 billion deal to supply meals to the Russian military, which would later fund the Wagner Group.

sections.heading: Wagner Group and Involvement in Ukraine
paragraphs: The Wagner Group, founded by Prigozhin in 2014, played a crucial role in supporting Russian separatist forces during the [[war-in-donbas|Donbas War]] and later in the 2022 [[full-scale-russo-ukrainian-war|invasion of Ukraine]]. The group was utilized to further Russian interests while providing the [[kremlin|Kremlin]] with plausible deniability.

Prigozhin publicly acknowledged his role in the Wagner Group, claiming it was established to protect Russian interests [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], particularly in response to the perceived genocide of the Russian population in the [[donbas|Donbas]] region.

sections.heading: Criticism and Rebellion
paragraphs: Throughout the conflict in Ukraine, Prigozhin criticized the Russian Defense Ministry for its handling of the war and the reasons given for the invasion. His discontent culminated in a brief rebellion against Russian military leadership in June 2023, during which Wagner forces captured Rostov-on-Don and advanced toward Moscow.
The rebellion was called off the following day, and Prigozhin relocated to Belarus after charges against him were dropped.

sections.heading: Death and Legacy
paragraphs: On 23 August 2023, Prigozhin died in a plane crash in Tver Oblast, north of Moscow, two months after his rebellion. Speculations regarding the cause of the crash suggest possible sabotage. His death marked the end of a controversial figure whose actions had significant implications for Russia's military operations in Ukraine.
